claim: Existing benchmark test suites are thin: HumanEval averages 7.7 tests/problem and MBPP 3, and EvalPlus's 80x more tests dropped pass rate by 15%, so measured pass rates (the execution ground truth) are inflated.
stance_target: L1/L4: execution ground truth quality and self-written test adequacy
quoted_support: Initial analyses of benchmarks like HumanEval [ 6 ] (avg. 7.7 tests/problem), MBPP [ 3 ] (3 tests/problem), and EvalPlus [ 27 , 28 ] (which saw a 15% pass rate drop with 80× more tests) indicate the fragility of current evaluation setups due to sparse test coverage.

claim: Evaluation suites with limited homogeneous test cases let subtle faults go undetected, inflating measured performance and corrupting RLVR reward estimates.
stance_target: execution labels are noisy proxies; false-pass rate must be treated as label noise in calibration studies
quoted_support: these evaluation suites often comprise only a limited number of homogeneous test cases, resulting in subtle faults going undetected.
